findings.reason: §2 widens what the reader accepts without extending the guard that shares its blind spot, and the plan should expose "the words this probe runs" once and have all five sites read it.
findings.text: the plan also leaves four other sites resolving "the program a probe runs" from `probe[0]` alone, so the interpreter case §2 teaches the reference reader to see through is still invisible to them — the no-op and printer head tests (recovery_wait.py:796-799), `_wait_probe_is_a_no_op` (recovery_wait.py:814), `_wait_probe_prints_structured_output` (recovery_liveness.py:856), `_wait_probe_job_id` (recovery_classification.py:495); the load-bearing one is the structured-output guard: `["python3","-c","...run(['sacct','--json','-j','1306915'],...).stdout..."]` is refused today only because the reference reader names nothing (§1 records exactly that refusal), and §2 makes it an accepted declaration while `_wait_probe_prints_structured_output` cannot see the `--json` inside the string — so the 2026-10-13 shape (last line `}`, no terminal state ever matched) is no longer refused where a one-line repair is possible and surfaces only later as a `_wait_observation_defect` reading on a parked run

findings.reason: §4 must either delete the wrapper and fold both forms into the owner, or say which shapes it keeps and why; as written the collapse is lossy and the plan's done-when does not cover it.
findings.text: §4 says `_wait_probe_job_id` "reads job ids through the reader §2 exposes", which makes it a one-line delegator at recovery_classification.py:517 and 566, but the function it would delegate to does not parse two forms it parses today — the glued `-j1306915` (recovery_classification.py:502-503) and the bare-digit fallback (504-506) — so either the function survives as a second reader that can drift from the owner, or `squeue -j1306915` silently stops naming its job

findings.reason: extend `_wait_probe_shell_words` (parameterised or widened, with its docstring saying why the interpreter set is the wider one) rather than adding a parallel splitter, so the two callers cannot disagree about how one string is worded.
findings.text: §2 splits an interpreter's code string "on whitespace and on `, [ ] ( ) ;`, then strips quotes from each word's edges", which is `_wait_probe_shell_words` with a wider separator set and a wider strip set; written as a new function it puts a second splitter in the same file over the same kind of string, and the shell case survives the wider set unchanged because `,`, `[` and `]` are not characters a shell reference word needs

findings.reason: against public_definitions 2360, cli_options 465, mcp_views 15 and refusal_families 23 the section must account for the surface it adds, and here it can account for it by retiring one definition and one duplicated refusal string rather than by growing either family.
findings.text: §2 adds a new module-level definition (the job-id reader) and rewrites a refusal message, and §3 adds two new entries to a public map (`RECOVERY_CLASSIFICATION_DUTY_KINDS`), while no section of §2, §3 or §4 names anything retired or merged or states why nothing can be; the nearest candidates are visible in the tree — the new reader can retire `_wait_probe_job_id` outright (recovery_classification.py:487) and the rewritten refusal can reuse `_WAIT_ACCEPTED_SHAPES` and `_SACCT_STATE_FORM` instead of spelling the accepted shapes a second time

findings.reason: naming the two constants turns a new string into a reference, which is a sentence of plan text and removes a drift the tree has already paid for once.
findings.text: §2 asks the refusal to name "the argument-vector shape (`["squeue","-h","-j","<id>"]` or a `sacct` vector)", which already exists twice in the tree — `_SACCT_STATE_FORM = "sacct -n -X -o State -j"` (recovery_liveness.py:841) and `_WAIT_ACCEPTED_SHAPES` (recovery_wait.py:215) — and the refusal §2 edits already appends `_WAIT_ACCEPTED_SHAPES` at recovery_liveness.py:1010; the plan cites neither, so a worker writing §2 will most likely hand-type a third spelling of the same advice

response_events.note: §2 now exposes one reader of the program a probe actually runs, seeing through shells and interpreters, used by the reference reader, the no-op and printer tests, _wait_probe_is_a_no_op, _wait_probe_prints_structured_output and the job-id reader; recovery_liveness.py joins its write paths.
§4 now deletes _wait_probe_job_id and folds its glued -j1306915 and bare-digit forms into §2's reader, with a case for the glued form.

deep_module-1.note: §2 now exposes one reader of the program a probe actually runs, seeing through shells and interpreters, used by the reference reader, the no-op and printer tests, _wait_probe_is_a_no_op, _wait_probe_prints_structured_output and the job-id reader; recovery_liveness.py joins its write paths.

thin_wrapper-1.note: §4 now deletes _wait_probe_job_id and folds its glued -j1306915 and bare-digit forms into §2's reader, with a case for the glued form.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the plan exposes a job-id reader but not the reading underneath it, "which program this probe actually runs", so the interpreter blindness §2 removes stays in place at every other site that takes `probe[0]` at face value.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 adds a second code-string splitter beside `_wait_probe_shell_words` (recovery_wait.py:744) instead of widening the one that exists.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 2360, cli_options 465, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 23; §2 adds one new module-level definition and a rewritten refusal, and no section states what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites the code it extends section by section, but it omits the sibling probe reader that already owns the sacct shape it proposes to recommend: `recovery_liveness._wait_probe_prints_structured_output` / `_SACCT_STATE_FORM` (recovery_liveness.py:841-855) and the shared refusal vocabulary `_WAIT_ACCEPTED_SHAPES` (recovery_wait.py:215), which the refusal §2 rewrites already appends at recovery_liveness.py:1010.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4 turns `_wait_probe_job_id` into a delegator over the new reader while leaving behind probe shapes only that function parses, and the plan does not say whether the function is deleted or keeps them.
